reviews.author: Nick
reviews.content: A masterclass in queer horror! Adrian Chiarella brilliantly subverts the conversion therapy trope by turning the "cleansing" ritual into a living, shape-shifting nightmare. The entity taking the shape of what the boys desire most—each other—is a devastatingly poetic metaphor. Tyson Perkins’ gorgeous, bleak cinematography of rural Australia makes every frame feel loaded with dread. It’s atmospheric, deeply romantic, and utterly heartbreaking.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content: If you have seen It Follows, then a lot of the beats of this movie will be familiar to you. This movie, however, is better than It Follows because it gives a context as to why it happens. The characters therefore become more relatable and the tension becomes more grounded than the jump scares of It Follows. The cast in this movie are doing a great job, and the director is doing fantastically. The effects are well produced and the indifference of certain side characters heighten the sense of abandonment that the characters suffer through. It's a good watch.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: There is something really quite horrific about this story, but it's not so much that we have anything going bump in the night - it's that a community's solution to two lads caught in a clinch is to subject them to something akin to an exorcism. "Ryan" (Stacy Clausen) is the hunky, tousled blond lad who has been becoming closer to "Naim" (Joe Bird). The latter lad appears much more impressionable and in pretty distraught when he finds his new-found love messing about with "Hunter" (Jeremy Blewitt) in his backyard. Desolate, he reports him to his parents. Their solution is to bring in a creepy "deliverance healer" (Nicholas Hope) who waves a cigarette lighter around for a while, quotes some distinctly ropey scripture, and then pronounes the boys cured! Except, well his definition of cure actually releases a malevolent spirit into their lives that adopts the appearance of the other and that will stop at nothing to destroy him. Initially, the boys have no idea that this menace is out to get them, but after a fearsomely violent encounter leads to tragedy, "Naim" finds his mother has signed him up for the same treatment - ostensibly to keep him safe. Hmmm - what chance now he and "Ryan" can tell friend from foe and stop it before it stops one of them? There are two really quite engaging performances here and what's more the pared-back style of the production does much of the heavy lifting without the need for special effects that the limited budget would never have been able to deliver adequately. Much of the sense of peril here is left to our own imagination and to some clever use of the photography to often quite menacingly juxtapose the camera and the characters - sometimes leaving us as uncertain as them as to who is who/real. It's quite a sad critique of small-town mentalities and of their reliance on religiosity to avoid facing what is real in the lives of their own offspring who just happen to be different from them, and though it could perhaps have spent a little more time developing the personas a bit more, it has an intimacy to it and is well worth ninety minutes as horror, like beauty, proves to be very much in the eye of the beholder.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Trapped in an isolated setting, two teenage boys must flee a relentless, violent entity that disguises itself as their deepest desire—each other.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: In a harrowing blend of horror, romance, and drama, two teenage boys find themselves hunted by a terrifying supernatural force. The creature preys on their unspoken feelings, transforming into the exact likeness of the person each boy desires most. As the lines between love and deception blur, they are forced to confront both the monster outside and their true emotions within. To survive the night, they must learn to distinguish real affection from a fatal illusion.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Leviticus follows two teenage best friends whose burgeoning romantic feelings for one another take a dark, supernatural turn during an isolated getaway. Their peaceful retreat shatters when a sinister, ancient entity begins stalking them from the surrounding woods. The creature possesses a insidious hunting tactic: it shapeshifts into the form of the individual its target desires above all else. Because both boys harbor secret, intense feelings for one another, the monster repeatedly takes on each boy's likeness to lure the other into deadly traps. Trust quickly unravels as neither teenager can be entirely sure if the person standing before them is his true love or a lethal phantom. As the attacks grow increasingly violent, the boys are forced to articulate their unspoken emotions to create safe words and emotional touchstones. Through a gauntlet of terror, psychological mind games, and physical threats, their bond is tested to its absolute limit. Ultimately, they must combine their resourcefulness and genuinely accept their affection for one another to outsmart the shape-shifting beast and make a desperate bid for freedom.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Leviticus is a chilling horror-drama that explores the delicate intersection of teenage desire and mortal peril. Centered on two long-time male friends grappling with covert romantic feelings, the story unfolds as they encounter an ancient, predatory entity capable of weaponizing human longing. By taking the shape of the person its prey desires most, the monster turns the boys' mutual affection into their greatest vulnerability. Blending atmospheric dread with a tender coming-of-age romance, the narrative delivers a suspenseful story about survival, identity, and the power of authentic connection in the face of absolute terror.

story_structure.climax: Cornered by the entity, the boys face a harrowing confrontation where recognizing the genuine truth of their bond is the only way to expose the monster and survive.
story_structure.conflict: A malevolent entity begins hunting the boys by shapeshifting into the object of their deepest desire—taking the exact form of each other to manipulate and destroy them.
story_structure.resolution: With the immediate threat overcome, the survivors are left to process the trauma of the ordeal and confront the now-undeniable reality of their feelings.
story_structure.introduction: Two teenage friends navigate their unspoken feelings for one another while trapped in an increasingly tense, isolated environment.
story_structure.risingAction: As the creature leverages their mutual attraction and trust to divide them, the boys must learn to distinguish the real friend from the monster while constantly on the run.

faq.answer: The film follows two teenage boys, Naim and Ryan, in a devoutly religious Australian town who develop feelings for each other. After a deliverance ritual is performed on them, they are stalked by a violent entity that shapeshifts into the person they desire most—each other.
faq.question: What is the plot overview of Leviticus?

faq.answer: The film stars Joe Bird as Naim and Stacy Clausen as Ryan, alongside Mia Wasikowska, Jeremy Blewitt, and Nicholas Hope.
faq.question: Who stars in Leviticus?

faq.answer: Leviticus was written and directed by Australian filmmaker Adrian Chiarella.
faq.question: Who directed and wrote Leviticus?

faq.answer: No, Leviticus is an original story created by writer-director Adrian Chiarella, though its title references the biblical Book of Leviticus and draws inspiration from real-world religious suppression.
faq.question: Is Leviticus based on a book or a true story?

faq.answer: The title refers to the Old Testament biblical Book of Leviticus, which contains strict moral and religious laws historically referenced regarding sin, purity rituals, and homosexuality.
faq.question: What is the significance of the title Leviticus?
